public_rationale: Part of this holds. CoreWeave's Q1 2025 results show the OpenAI deal added $11.2 billion of backlog. Other contracted backlog slipped from $15.1 billion to $14.7 billion. So nearly all new contracted demand at that point came from OpenAI. But 'entirely' goes too far. CoreWeave also cited other customer wins, including an IBM partnership, and bought Weights & Biases. About 57% of its backlog was non-OpenAI contracts, mostly Microsoft. Nothing public shows all of Microsoft's usage served OpenAI. Zitron himself softened it to 'largely (if not entirely)'. Largely holds; entirely is not shown.
limitations: Microsoft's split between its own and OpenAI's workloads at CoreWeave is unknown. If it were all for OpenAI, the claim would be closer to true.
Backlog is one measure of expansion; physical capacity buildout by customer is not disclosed.

from_speaker: largely (if not entirely) for the benefit of OpenAI
our_interpretation: 'Expansion' read as CoreWeave's growth in contracted demand (backlog) and capacity around April 2025.
'Entirely' read plainly as all or nearly all. Microsoft's usage counts toward OpenAI only to the extent evidence shows it served OpenAI.
Target period is Q1 2025 through the post date, the latest period CoreWeave reported on.
criteria.support_condition: CoreWeave disclosures show its new contracted demand and capacity expansion came all or nearly all from OpenAI, directly or through Microsoft.
criteria.contradiction_condition: CoreWeave disclosures show substantial expansion tied to customers other than OpenAI or OpenAI-related Microsoft work.
